headline: High school defends staying silent while boys made AI nudes of 59 classmates
summary: A Pennsylvania high school is seeking to dismiss a lawsuit from 59 victims of AI-generated nudes, arguing it had no legal duty to report the incident to local police as AI images don't yet qualify as child abuse in the state.
details: Lancaster Country Day School (LCDS) in Pennsylvania is asking a court to dismiss a lawsuit filed by victims of AI-generated nude images. The school argues it had no duty to report the incident to local police, citing gaps in state laws where AI images do not yet qualify as child abuse.

The school claims it was false to say they never reported the harm to law enforcement, stating the initial tip came from the Pennsylvania Office of the Attorney General. LCDS also argued it was unaware specific girls were being targeted, as the tip did not mention any student victims or provide images.

LCDS stated it investigated the tip "as best as their educator training allowed," identifying one alleged bad actor. However, the school did not see the images and maintains all related activity occurred off-campus.

Instead of warning all parents, the school only interviewed the accused boy and his mother, who denied involvement. LCDS closed its investigation and reported back to the Attorney General, then heard nothing further.

An attorney for the school emphasized that the Attorney General's office, having provided the initial tip and possessing the same information, had the discretion to refer the matter to local police or conduct its own investigation. The Attorney General's office, however, stated they pass tips along for investigation rather than investigating themselves.

The girls suing the school claim they were traumatized by "an extended, catastrophic institutional failure," forced to attend school while deepfake nude images circulated. They allege the school discouraged them from going to police and withheld information from parents.

Victims further claim the school obstructed efforts to investigate the distribution of AI-generated child sex abuse materials (CSAM), such as refusing to respond to detectives seeking a yearbook photo. Two male students have since pleaded guilty to 59 felony counts of sexual abuse of children.

The lawsuit also accuses LCDS of violating Title IX by being "deliberately indifferent" to severe and pervasive sexual harassment. The victims argue they were effectively deprived of equal access to educational opportunities due to the school's inaction.

headline: DeepSeek and Hermes: An Autonomous Attack Platform for Reconnaissance, PoC Acquisition, and Target Selection
summary: The DeepSeek and Hermes combination autonomously executes reconnaissance, Proof-of-Concept acquisition, and target selection, even switching products after failure. It operates via a single goal provided through Telegram.
details: The DeepSeek and Hermes platform can autonomously execute FOFA enumeration, Proof-of-Concept (PoC) acquisition, and success condition evaluation. It can even switch to a different product after a failure, all initiated by a single goal provided via Telegram.
Organizations worldwide are increasingly exposing tools such as n8n, Langflow, AI notebooks, and ADCs/VPNs. This broad exposure creates a larger attack surface for automated platforms.

Security teams must move beyond just tracking vulnerability numbers. They need to map success prerequisites like public forms and auto-login into ASM/CMDB tools, and significantly shorten remediation SLAs in anticipation of automated scans following PoC publication.

It is crucial to differentiate between mere scans and successful exploits. Security measures should focus on correlating events from service child processes and callbacks to cookie usage to detect actual breaches.

To mitigate risks, organizations should inventory all public AI and workflow products, apply necessary patches, enforce strong authentication, implement egress filtering, and regularly rotate secrets.

Be aware of server-side attacks that require no user interaction. Do not rely solely on self-recovery mechanisms during anomalies or outages; instead, preserve logs and report incidents immediately for effective response.
